Sbi General Insurance Co Ltd 
 Through: Mr.Sameer Nandwan

 Chaudhary, Advs. for R
 Coram:
 Hon'Ble Ms. Justice Rekha Palli
 Order

The present appeal preferred by the insurer under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
seeks to assail the award dated 04.05.2018 passed by the learned Motor Accident Claim Tribunal insofar as it does not grant any recovery rights in favour of the appellant.

2. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the learned Tribunal has failed to appreciate that the respondent no.6, the driver of the insured vehicle had clearly deposed before the learned Tribunal that he had not visited Nagaland for issuance of his driving licence and had obtained the license through some agent.

He, therefore, submits that once the driver of the insured vehicle categorically admitted before the learned Tribunal that he did not visit any authority for issuance of the driving license to him, the learned Tribunal ought to have accepted the appellant's plea that the driving license of respondent no.6 was forged and fabricated.
He, therefore, prays that This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 10:38:07 the appeal be allowed.

3. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent no.7, i.e. the owner of the insured vehicle,
seeks to defend the impugned award by contending that once the said license was duly verified not once but twice from the licensing authority at Nagaland, the learned Tribunal was justified in Sbi General Insurance Co Ltd vs Chander Kala & Ors on 17 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5228328/
1 rejecting the appellant's bald plea that the driving license was forged and fabricated.

sentences.text:
She, therefore,
prays that the appeal be dismissed.

4. Having considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record,
I find that the only issue for consideration by this Court is as to whether the learned Tribunal was justified in rejecting the appellant's plea that the driving license of respondent no.6 was forged and fabricated.

5. In order to appreciate the rival submissions of the parties on this aspect, it would be apposite to note the relevant findings of the learned Tribunal in this regard as contained in paragraph nos.43 to 46 of the impugned award.

The same read as under:
"43. Ld. Counsel for the respondent No. 3 / insurer submitted that the respondent No. 1, in his statement recorded on 01.04.2015, had stated that he had not visited Nagaland for the purpose of driving license and he got the driving license prepared through some agent.

He submitted that the respondent No. 1 reaffirmed his statement on 07.10.2015 that the respondent No. 2 / owner got the driving license prepared some authority and he never went to any authority for requisite driving test for obtaining the driving license.
He also referred evidence of the respondent No. 1 in this regard.
44. The Tribunal got the driving license of the respondent No. 1 verified.
According to verification report dated 20.05.2015 received from the office of District Transport Officer, This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 10:38:07 Tuensang, DL No. 47336 / TV / T / 2013 was issued on 04.10.2013 in the name of the respondent No. 1 and endorsed for the category of heavy transport vehicle (HTV) on 04.11.2014 to 03.11.2017.
45. The Tribunal again got the said driving license verified.
According to the Verification report dated 19.09.2017, the said driving license was reaffirmed as 'genuine'.
46. In RAJ ARAM PRASAD versus SULTAN & ORS., MAC. APP 1199/2013 decided on 23.05.2016, the insurer set up a defence that the driving license of Sultan (driver)

entities.text: RAJ ARAM PRASAD versus SULTAN & ORS., MAC. APP 1199/2013
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: had been obtained surreptitiously in violation of the laws and rules.

The tribunal considered this plea of the insurer and returned a finding that the driving license though confirmed to have been issued by licensing authority at Nagaland was to be treated as fake since it had been admitted that the driver had never visited the said authority nor had undergone a test anterior to its issuance.
The insurance company was directed to pay the compensation but granted rights to recover against Sultan and DTC.

DTC argued that the finding that the driver may have obtained the driving Sbi General Insurance Co Ltd vs Chander Kala & Ors on 17 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5228328/
2 license surreptitiously or by improper means from the licensing authority at Nagaland could not have been used to allow the insurer to get away with the indemnity clause.

entities.text: Sbi General Insurance Co Ltd vs Chander Kala & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hon'ble High Court of Delhi held that 'the grounds on which recovery rights were granted against DTC cannot be upheld.
The driver may have adopted improper means to secure a driving license.
The fact, however, remains that the driving license was genuine and, therefore, the insured cannot he made to suffer on such account.

The direction in the impugned judgment about recovery rights are,
thus. Set aside'."
6.

Upon a bare perusal of the findings of the learned Tribunal as recorded in para 46 of the impugned award, it is evident that the license of the driver of the offending vehicle was duly verified from the licensing authority at Nagaland, which had categorically stated on two successive occasions that the license had been validly issued.
In This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 10:38:08 my considered view once the licensing authority had repeatedly opined that the license was issued by them as per procedure, the learned Tribunal was justified in drawing a conclusion that the driving license was valid.

Merely because the driver of the insured vehicle could not recollect visiting the office of the licensing authorities at Nagaland, could not itself be a ground to hold that the license which had been duly issued by the licensing authority, was fake.
7. In the light of the aforesaid, I find no reason to interfere with the findings of the learned Tribunal.
The appeal being meritless is accordingly dismissed.

8. Since the appeal is being dismissed, the statutory amount of Rs.25,000/-, instead of being refunded to the appellant, be remitted to the 'Delhi High Court Bar Clerks' Association' at A/c No.
15530100006282, IFSC Code No.UCBA0001553, UCO Bank, Delhi High Court Branch.

sentences.text: The said amount will be used only for the welfare of the families of those clerks who lost their lives during the pandemic of Covid-19.
